findings.text: Guest instruction operand descriptor distinguishes register and memory forms including string memory alongside immediate and several vector widths plus an empty form. It records transfer size with repeat count and keeps both original and current scalar payloads in overlapping storage. Addressing offers register reference and segmented effective address with selector plus vector indices. A wide aligned value area accommodates scalar and pointer plus vector payloads.

Instruction fetch staging uses a byte array sized for the longest legal instruction with cursors for current position and end. Separate input output and memory staging each use a one kilobyte array with position and end offsets for buffered guest transfers.
Longest emulated instruction span is fifteen bytes.

Emulation context joins virtual processor identity with operation hooks and snapshots of flags and instruction pointer plus execution mode. It tracks interruptibility after special moves and permission bypass with single step state and exception details plus optional guest physical address. Decode area records opcode shape and intercept identity with prefix and size details and register validity and dirtiness maps and addressing and branch hint. Trailing area holds source pair with destination and memory operands alongside general register file and fetch plus data staging.
Emulator general register file holds sixteen entries in one build variant and eight entries in the other variant.
Emulated processor mode is one of real and virtual 8086 and 16 bit protected and 32 bit protected and 64 bit long. Selection is per instruction context with no implied ordering among modes.
String repeat prefix for equal compare is byte value F3 and for not equal compare is byte value F2.

Emulated vendor identification words for the common AMD string place 68747541 in the first register and 444D4163 in the second register and 69746E65 in the third register. The alternate AMD string uses 69444D41 then 21726574 then 74656273 in the same register order.
Vendor words for the Hygon string are 6F677948 then 656E6975 then 6E65476E in register order. Vendor words for the Intel string are 756E6547 then 6C65746E then 49656E69 in the same order.
Vendor words for the Centaur string are 746E6543 then 736C7561 then 48727561 in register order.

Interception staging starts at a none value chosen so zero initialization matches nothing and then offers before exception and after exception and after memory access points. Reasons cover control register and debug register traffic and descriptor table management and timer and counter reads and flag and identification operations and virtualization lifecycle and interrupt control and power waits and translation invalidation and model specific register plus port traffic.
Emulation result codes are negative one for failure and zero for success and one for restart request and two for host intercepted handling.
An emulation attempt ends failed or completed or restart requested or intercepted. Restart and intercepted are non error continuations that require further host action rather than simple success.
Remote flush range record carries a starting guest frame number with a page count that guides construction of a guest mapping flush list.

Remote translation flush keeps a cached common root to avoid scanning on every request. A valid cached root flushes once on a fast path. An invalid cached root triggers a scan over virtual processors that adopts the first valid root seen and flushes each distinct valid root a single time. The cache is retained only when at most one distinct valid root appeared during the scan. Multiple distinct valid roots leave the cache marked invalid. Range requests build a list through a fill helper while full requests flush without a list.
Exposes range based remote translation flush built from start frame and page count with delegation to an internal range flusher, plus full remote flush that delegates with no range.
Exposes root tracking that records the calling virtual processor root and invalidates the cached common root on mismatch, active only while Hyper-V remote flush is the selected flush implementation.
Common root cache with per processor root values is protected by the Hyper-V root table lock across both the flush scan with cache update and the tracking update with invalidation test.

Partition assist page is allocated lazily as one zeroed page per virtual machine shared by all virtual processors to meet Hyper-V direct flush prerequisites. Allocation failure yields the invalid page marker. Success yields the physical address of the shared page. Current logic reserves the page for compliance without consuming its contents.
Fallback definitions without Hyper-V support report operation not supported from remote flush and perform no action for root tracking.
Emulated local APIC version is hex 14 and its memory mapped window spans 4096 bytes.
Timer advance calibration bounds are 100 cycles minimum and 10000 cycles maximum with step 8. Initial advance is 1000 nanoseconds with a 5000 nanosecond ceiling.

Timer advance assistance starts enabled and vector hashing starts enabled. Paravirtual end of interrupt attention uses bit one. Virtual APIC check constant is zero. The static key recording presence of a virtual processor without an APIC starts false.

Local vector entry masks preserve masked state with pending delivery and vector number. Local interrupt variants also preserve delivery mode with input polarity and remote request state plus level trigger mode. The static per entry mask table assigns timer and thermal and counter and local interrupt pair and error and check interrupt entries accordingly, with timer mode added at run time.

Extended APIC logical destination is derived from the identifier by moving upper identifier bits to the high half and setting one low bit chosen by the low four identifier bits. Setting an extended identifier writes both identifier and logical destination registers and marks the APIC address map dirty with release ordering, warning if the supplied identifier differs from the virtual processor identifier.

Local vector entry count is maximal when machine check capability advertises corrected check interrupts and one less otherwise. After capability change the logic masks any newly exposed entries and refreshes the version register. No work occurs when the kernel APIC is absent or the count is unchanged.

Posted interrupt harvesting merges pending words into interrupt request registers word by word with atomic compare exchange retry and computes highest set vector overall. It reports whether the overall highest vector originated from the newly merged posted bits. The per processor wrapper additionally latches a software pending flag when the highest came from posted bits but hardware acceleration is inactive. Empty posted state only refreshes the highest vector from existing registers.

Posted merge uses unsynchronized read with compare exchange retry per register word, so concurrent mergers may retry and intermediate register views may be stale. Callers must rely only on the returned highest vector and new from posted indication rather than assuming a stable snapshot.

Paravirtual interrupt delivery validates that destination shorthand and mode control bits are clear and derives vector with delivery mode and level plus trigger from the control word. It then delivers to physical map targets selected by low and high bitmap clusters offset from a minimum identifier, advancing the minimum by cluster width between clusters. It reports invalid argument for bad control and not supported when no address map exists, otherwise the count delivered.
Physical APIC map lookup for paravirtual delivery is performed under a read side critical section that spans both low and high cluster walks without blocking or mutation.

Bitmap walks reject a minimum identifier beyond the map maximum and clamp each walk to the smaller of machine word width and remaining identifier space. Physical map indexing uses speculation hardening to bound the index.

Paravirtual end of interrupt uses a guest byte holding enabled or disabled values accessed through cached mappings plus a host attention bit. Enabling writes the enabled value to the guest and sets the attention bit. Test and clear reads the guest byte and masks to enabled state, writes disabled back when previously enabled, always clears the attention bit, and reports prior enabled state. Guest access failure yields a safe false or early return without changing attention incorrectly.

Cached guest writes first validate total length against the cached extent and refresh the host mapping when slot generation changed. Erroneous host address fails. Missing memslot falls back to an uncached guest write by physical address. Otherwise data is copied to the cached host mapping at the requested offset and the backing slot page is marked dirty.
Exposes cached guest memory write with an offset variant as the primitive and a plain variant that delegates with zero offset.
Length plus offset beyond cached extent triggers a one time warning and invalid argument failure. Host copy shortfall surfaces as bad address rather than partial success.

Memory mapped APIC window accepts only addresses from base inclusive to base plus length exclusive. Outside addresses report not supported. When hardware enable is off or extended mode is active, behavior depends on a memory hole quirk, either reporting not supported or returning all ones without touching registers. Otherwise the request dispatches to register read logic with length aware handling.

Read intercept disable mask for extended APIC exposes all software readable registers except the current timer count, which remains intercepted because software emulation owns the timer value. Invocation without an in kernel APIC warns once and returns zero.

Timer interrupt presence treats protected guest APIC state as already injected. Otherwise with hardware enabled it tests the timer vector in service state normally and in request state when acceleration is active. Expiry waiting requires kernel APIC with expired deadline plus nonzero advance and an injected timer interrupt. Hypervisor timer use is false without kernel APIC and otherwise reflects the per timer in use flag.
Accelerated end of interrupt handling forwards the vector to input output APIC completion and requests event processing for the owning virtual processor.
Processor priority refresh recomputes priority from current APIC state and interrupt request clear removes the specified vector from pending state.
APIC address map freshness cycles among clean and update in progress and dirty. Identifier updates publish dirty state so readers rebuild the map.
Input output device callbacks obtain the enclosing APIC instance through container linkage from the device member without extra lookup.
Exposes machine check capability follow up that adjusts local vector count, plus posted interrupt merge into request state, plus single vector clear and priority refresh operations.
Exposes accelerated end of interrupt completion with timer expiry waiting and hypervisor timer query plus extended APIC read intercept mask computation.
Exposes paravirtual fan out interrupt delivery across a physical APIC map selected by bitmaps and minimum identifier.

Reads that hit the disabled or extended mode path must not expose stale register contents. Quirk disabled behavior surfaces as not supported for pass through, while quirk enabled behavior returns all ones. Extended intercept query without kernel APIC must be treated as no disable rather than a valid mask.

Emulation operation hooks cover NMI mask control with SMM query and exit plus triple fault notification and extended control register access. Address helpers provide untagged guest virtual translation with canonical address testing and guest physical page validation.
Fast operation is a callback receiving a fast operation descriptor. Log output prefixes messages with the module name. The Hyper-V header uses an include guard to prevent double inclusion.
Vector counting walks the bitmap in register sized steps and sums population counts to report how many vectors are set, used for diagnostics of pending state.
